know.title: What to know before you go
know.space.title: Give wildlife space
know.space.body: Stay at least {small} m from deer, moose and elk, and {big} m from bears, wolves, coyotes and cougars.
know.feed.title: Never feed wildlife
know.feed.body: It’s illegal, and so is leaving food or garbage out. You can be charged under the Canada National Parks Act.
know.dogs.title: Dogs on a leash, always
know.dogs.body: It’s the law in every Parks Canada place, and it prevents dangerous wildlife encounters.
know.fires.title: Fires in fire boxes only
know.fires.body: Use the designated metal fire boxes and the firewood provided, and never leave a fire unattended.
know.fireBan.title: A fire ban is posted: no campfires
know.fireBan.body: While the ban is in effect, don’t light a campfire. Open the bulletin to see where it applies and what’s still allowed, such as some portable stoves.
know.firesRemote.title: Check the park’s fire rules
know.firesRemote.body: Remote and northern parks set their own rules for fires and fuel, so check the park’s page and bulletins before you go.
know.drones.title: Leave the drone at home
know.drones.body: Drones are prohibited in all Parks Canada places without a permit, and fines can reach {fine}.
know.911.title: Call 911 in an emergency
know.911.body: Cell coverage isn’t reliable in the backcountry or remote areas, so leave a trip plan with someone.
